title: OCDH advocacy after alleged police-torture deaths
reason: The captured report documents a human-rights appeal/engagement with police, not a public protest or mass gathering.
notes: The alleged death and torture claims are attributed to OCDH/family accounts. No attendance or street mobilization is described; advocacy and alleged state abuse are not themselves a protest event.

title: OCDH press conference on police abuses and youths’ deaths
reason: The source reports a press conference, with no evidence of a public protest gathering or at least 50 participants.
notes: The issue extraction discusses abuses and two deaths after police beatings. These allegations are not coded as a protest absent evidence of a protest action.

title: Mathias Dzon press conference and call for democratic unity
reason: The source documents a party-headquarters press conference and political statement, not a public protest or mass gathering.
notes: Issue 4108 reports a position on constitutional revision and a call to unite democrats; no street action or attendance is described.

title: SACER report of alleged para-commando unrest and planned palace march
reason: The single-source account describes alleged military/coup activity and an intended seizure of power, not a documented public mass protest; armed action is outside the protest coding scope.
notes: SACER attributes the report to unnamed sources. No independent contemporary confirmation or actual public assembly was found in the scoped search pass; retain as unverified context, not an event.

title: SOPECO workers’ indefinite sit-in over salary arrears
reason: Vox Congo retrospectively dates the sit-in’s launch to Feb. 7, 2022, outside this January unit.
notes: RFI/Journal Africa reported in March that at least 241 employees were in a sit-in lasting more than a month; Vox Congo later supplies the Feb. 7 onset. Do not move the activity into January based only on the March report’s duration.

title: E2C electricity-service march in Brazzaville
reason: The reported action was scheduled and attempted on Apr. 8, 2022, outside this January unit.
notes: SACER reports the prefectural ban; Les Échos reports that organizers attempted the march and were briefly detained and released, with no large mobilization. These April accounts are retained as boundary evidence only.
